# S72 — Reading a webhook handler that lost bookings and reported success

**Concept:** spreading `undefined` does not throw — and three review-passing lines that together fabricate data while deleting real records.

This is the first session of the *second pass*: every Phase 1 topic has now been covered at least once, so instead of new material the sessions get harder and interleaved — several concepts mixed into one encounter, unlabelled.

**Scenario.** A tour booking office takes reservations from a partner over a webhook. A PR generated by an AI assistant shipped, described as "partner webhook handling + retry, ready to deploy". It compiles, passes the happy path and throws nothing. Then the partner had a two-hour outage. The owner calls: *"there are six one-person bookings with no deposit that nobody made, and four real ones are missing."*

## Encounter 1 — eight Phase 1 traps in a row

```js
const DOMYSLNE = { osoby: 1, zaliczka: 0, waluta: "ISK", anulowane: false };

function normalizuj(payload) {
  return { ...DOMYSLNE, ...payload };
}

const a = normalizuj({ osoby: 4, zaliczka: 0 });
console.log("1)", a.zaliczka, a.waluta);

const b = normalizuj({ osoby: 2, waluta: undefined });
console.log("2)", b.waluta, "| klucz obecny:", "waluta" in b);

function wymagaZaliczki(r) {
  return r.osoby >= 4 || r.kwota > 50000 && r.waluta === "ISK";
}
console.log("3)", wymagaZaliczki({ osoby: 2, kwota: 80000, waluta: "EUR" }));
console.log("4)", wymagaZaliczki({ osoby: 4, kwota: 0, waluta: "EUR" }));

const znane = [101, 102, 103];
console.log("5)", znane.includes("102"), znane.indexOf(102));

const wolne = 0;
console.log("6)", wolne || "brak danych", "|", wolne ?? "brak danych");

const ceny = [9, 80, 1000, 20];
const top = ceny.sort().slice(0, 2);
console.log("7)", top, "| oryginal:", ceny);

function sprawdz(r) {
  if (!r.vsk) throw new Error("brak VSK");
  return true;
}
let ok = "nie ustawiono";
try {
  [{ vsk: "IS1" }, { vsk: "" }, { vsk: "IS3" }].forEach((r) => sprawdz(r));
  ok = true;
} catch (e) {
  ok = "zlapane: " + e.message;
}
console.log("8)", ok);
```

## Encounter 2 — the AI-generated PR

```js
const przyjete = new Set();

async function pobierzZPartnera(id) {
  const res = await fetch(`https://api.partner.is/bookings/${id}`);
  if (res.status !== 200) throw new Error("HTTP " + res.status);
  return res.json();
}

async function obsluzWebhook(body) {
  if (przyjete.has(body.id)) return { status: "duplikat" };
  przyjete.add(body.id);

  let dane;
  for (let proba = 0; proba < 3; proba++) {
    try {
      dane = await pobierzZPartnera(body.id);
      break;
    } catch (e) {
      console.log("  proba", proba, "padla:", e.message);
    }
  }

  const rekord = { ...DOMYSLNE, ...dane, id: body.id };
  if (rekord.osoby > 0 && rekord.zaliczka >= 0) {
    return { status: "zapisane", rekord };
  }
  return { status: "odrzucone" };
}
```

Traced with the partner down (`fetch` stubbed to return `503` every time):

```txt
A) obsluzWebhook({ id: 77 })      first delivery, during the outage
B) obsluzWebhook({ id: 77 })      partner recovered and RETRIES
C) obsluzWebhook({ id: "77" })    same number, arrived as a string
```

## Verified

Run on `node v24.13.1` before writing any answer key. Encounter 2 was run with `fetch` replaced by a stub returning `503`; the rest of the code is byte for byte identical.

```txt
1) 0 ISK
2) undefined | klucz obecny: true
3) false
4) true
5) false 1
6) brak danych | 0
7) [ 1000, 20 ] | oryginal: [ 1000, 20, 80, 9 ]
8) zlapane: brak VSK

A)   proba 0 padla: HTTP 503
A)   proba 1 padla: HTTP 503
A)   proba 2 padla: HTTP 503
A) -> {"status":"zapisane","rekord":{"osoby":1,"zaliczka":0,"waluta":"ISK","anulowane":false,"id":77}}
B) -> {"status":"duplikat"}
C) -> {"status":"zapisane","rekord":{"osoby":1,"zaliczka":0,"waluta":"ISK","anulowane":false,"id":"77"}}

control: { ...DOMYSLNE, ...undefined } -> {"osoby":1,"zaliczka":0,"waluta":"ISK","anulowane":false}  (does not throw)
```

## Answer key

Both halves of the complaint come from **one** bug seen from two sides.

After three failed attempts `break` never runs, so `dane` stays `undefined`. The line `{ ...DOMYSLNE, ...dane, id: body.id }` **does not throw** — spreading `undefined` (or `null`) is legal and simply contributes no properties. The record comes out with a full set of defaults, and the guard `rekord.osoby > 0 && rekord.zaliczka >= 0` passes *precisely because* the defaults are `1` and `0`. Hence the bookings nobody made.

`przyjete.add(body.id)` runs **before** any success, so a failed run still leaves a mark. When the partner retries after fixing its outage, the handler answers `duplikat` without a single attempt. Hence the missing real bookings — the same line causes both symptoms.

`Set` compares with SameValueZero, so `77` and `"77"` are two distinct entries. One type change in the payload and the dedupe is bypassed entirely.

Four defects worth blocking the PR over:

1. no `if (!dane) throw` guard after the retry loop — the only line that turns silent fabrication into a loud failure at the point of cause;
2. `add` before success instead of after it (or inside the same transaction as the write) — a dedupe turned into a redelivery blocker;
3. an unnormalised dedupe key (`String(body.id)`) — the guard is type-sensitive while the payload is not;
4. `res.status !== 200` treats `201`/`204` as failures and `404` the same as `429`, and the loop retries with no delay at all — that is not a retry, it is tripling traffic into a server that is already falling over.

Fix (1) first. While the code fabricates records, every other fix only changes *how many* bad rows reach the database.

A deliberate counterpoint to the previous session: `return` inside a `forEach` callback does not leave the enclosing function, but `throw` from the same callback **does** propagate through `forEach` into the outer `catch` (line `8`). Same construct, two keywords, opposite behaviour.

## Quiz

1. A webhook must be idempotent, yet the sender also retries when *your* handler failed. Where exactly should the dedupe key be written so both hold at once — and what about a run that crashed after the database write?
2. You see `if (res.status !== 200) throw`. Give three HTTP situations where that single line misbehaves, and say for each whether the failure is loud or silent.
3. `{ ...A, ...B }`, `A ?? B`, `A || B` and `function f(x = B)` all look like "supply a default". For `undefined`, `null` and `0`, say which substitute `B` and which let the original through.

**Answers.** (1) After a *successful* write, ideally in the same transaction, with the key as a `UNIQUE` column rather than an in-process `Set` — a `Set` dies on restart and does nothing across two instances. On retry, detect the key and return the *same* result as the first time: retries should be safe, not blocked. (2) `201`/`204` — a valid response treated as failure (loud but false; retrying something that succeeded risks a double write upstream). `404` — a permanent error retried three times for nothing, then ending as a silent defaults-only record. `429` — the one case where retrying is right, but it needs `Retry-After`, so three immediate attempts guarantee three more `429`s (silent). And the one that eats half of all integrations: `fetch` does not throw on `4xx`/`5xx` at all — only on network errors. (3) Spread: `B === undefined` lets `A` through untouched, but a *key* holding `undefined` inside `B` deletes the field from `A`. `??` substitutes for `undefined` and `null`, passes `0`. `||` substitutes for `undefined`, `null` **and** `0` (plus `""`, `NaN`, `false`). A parameter default fires **only** for `undefined` — `null` and `0` go through.

## Card added

**Q:** What does `{ ...A, ...B }` do when `B` is `undefined`, and why is that dangerous?

**A:** It throws nothing and adds no properties, so the result is plain `A` — i.e. defaults only. Fed with `dane` from a failed `fetch`, that produces a record which looks valid and passes validation instead of an error. The mirror case is the opposite: `{ key: undefined }` *deletes* the default. Rule: spreading `undefined` is a no-op, a key holding `undefined` is a deletion. Guard with `if (!dane) throw` before merging.

## Takeaway

In a year nobody will pay for writing these thirty lines; a model writes them in five seconds. They will pay for the sentence "this can't ship — during a partner outage it writes defaults and blocks the retry", said *before* the customer calls.
